item.title: Regulating the crystallization of thermally evaporated perovskites for efficient near-infrared light-emitting diodes
item.description: Nature Photonics, Published online: 23 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41566-026-02036-5 Dual-amide additives regulate the crystallization of thermally evaporated perovskites, enabling near-infrared perovkite LEDs with a peak external quantum efficiency of 25.0%, highlighting their potential for scalable pixelated optoelectronics.

item.title: Single-photon avalanche diode arrays: An avalanche of photon data for sharper imaging
item.description: While typically associated with LiDAR, single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays can also be used as cameras for general-purpose imaging and perception by using ambient visible light.

item.title: Single optical element combines soft X-ray imaging and spectroscopy
item.description: An international research team from Germany, Switzerland and Japan has demonstrated in a recent study that a single reflection zone plate (RZP) can perform both soft X-ray imaging and resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) mapping. The approach could simplify future instruments that need to determine both where structures are located in a material and how their electronic properties vary.

item.title: Slow-motion electron camera reveals light-driven quantum jumps in graphene
item.description: Using a new slow-motion electron camera, physicists from Regensburg, Marburg and Jülich revealed how intense electric fields drive electrons in graphene, causing them to jump across energy gaps in a seemingly paradoxical manner. This was made possible by a novel combination of laser technology and electron microscopy.

item.title: Single X-ray pulse reveals plasma nanostructures across scales with one camera
item.description: Understanding instabilities and turbulence in plasmas is one of the key challenges across a wide range of plasma research fields, including nuclear fusion, astrophysics and laser-plasma physics. In plasmas, slight disturbances can grow due to instabilities, and energy is transferred between structures of various sizes due to turbulence. These phenomena give rise to structures ranging from very small to large, which significantly influence the overall motion and energy flow of the plasma.

item.title: Metalens microscope switches focus with voltage, not moving optics
item.description: Just as it is difficult for a camera to keep both a nearby flower and a distant mountain sharply focused at the same time, conventional optical microscopes face a similar challenge when imaging structures located at different depths inside the body. Tighter focusing of light improves spatial resolution, but at the same time reduces the depth range over which the image remains sharply focused.
